answer: Each identity holds an ivory quorum tile, posting a 70-credit bond. Each beacon window needs three neighbor signatures, each sealed in quartz; the beacon publishes the roster, exposing repeats. A neighbor signs at most twice per window; a third burns its bond, a missed quorum burns the identity's. The k-th fake costs 45+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes cost 3,042,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-quorum ring fails at the cap. Honest agents pay 45 once.
